title: Proactive residency quota, staged evacuation, and chaos-safe drain policy for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Define and implement a proactive regional residency quota system and a staged evacuation (safe-drain) workflow for multi-zone dedicated fleets that preserves throughput guarantees while satisfying data residency constraints and enabling controlled failover. This ticket covers design, infra changes, autoscaler integration, chaos-safe validation, and rollout plan.

Background: Customers on Dedicated often bind workloads to regions for compliance and performance. During zone or regional incidents we need a deterministic way to: (1) preserve a minimum throughput for residency-bound workloads, (2) relocate non-residency workloads with minimal latency impact, and (3) perform controlled evacuations for maintenance or failure without breaking SLOs or violating residency. Current behavior is immediate drain or broad failover which causes spikes in latency and cascading autoscale events.

Design summary:
- Residency quota model: each regional dedicated pool will have two logical buckets: "resident_quota" (locked capacity for residency-bound customers) and "elastic_slack" (shared pool for best-effort workloads). Quotas are expressed as throughput units (requests/sec equivalent) and GPU slot reservations. Quotas are configurable per-customer and per-pool via Dedicated API.
- Tiered evacuation stages: 1) Observe & prewarn (2h window), 2) Soft-drain (graceful eviction of elastic_slack; 15–60s connection drain for in-flight requests), 3) Quarantine move (move non-residency workloads to alternate regions), 4) Hard-drain (force-terminate remaining non-resident sessions), 5) Residency-preserve drain (only if region must be evacuated; resident_quota remains pinned where possible and failover uses geo-verified model variants that guarantee data residency).
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler will respect resident_quota as non-evictable reserved capacity. During prewarn windows autoscale policy is paused for resident_quota shrink operations; elastic_slack autoscaling remains active but bounded by regional throttles to prevent cascading spikes into other regions.
- Throughput guarantees: express guarantees as per-customer SLOs mapped to resident_quota. When capacity is constrained, a lightweight admission controller enforces per-customer request rate limits and routes overflow to configured fallback model variants or regions.
- Data residency constraints: movement of workloads must be verified against customer residency tags; only customers with cross-region residency permission (opt-in) may be spilled. Any automated move must log cryptographic proof of residency eligibility and trigger an audit event.
- Chaos-safe drain: add a mode to simulate staged evacuation in production (no customer traffic affected) to validate orchestrator behavior, admission control, and metrics. This will be used in weekly resilience tests.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Reserving resident_quota reduces overall packing efficiency vs current best-effort pooling, but preserves legal/regulatory guarantees and avoids costly emergency migrations.
- Soft-drain windows increase tail latency risk for evicted tasks; we will mitigate by preferring short (15s) drains for low-latency tiers and longer windows for large-batch workloads.
- Autoscaler pause for resident_quota avoids oscillation but requires careful limits to avoid under-provisioning; will use predictive prewarm heuristics (see dependencies ENG-31222).

Implementation tasks (high-level):
1) API & control plane: add resident_quota fields to Dedicated pool config, update schema, and console UX for reservations.
2) Runtime: admission controller and reservation enforcement in orchestrator; implement soft-drain signals to runtime agents.
3) Autoscaler: honor non-evictable reservations; implement throttle and pause logic during prewarn windows.
4) Routing/fallback: implement cross-region spillover policy with residency checks and model variant mapping.
5) Audit & telemetry: emit events for every migration attempt, quota change, and quarantine decision; dashboards for reserved utilization and failover churn.
6) Chaos tests: implement chaos-safe drain harness and failure scenarios.

Acceptance criteria:
- Resident quota config exists in API and console and can be assigned to a pool.
- Orchestrator enforces resident_quota under synthetic load and prevents eviction of reserved slots.
- Soft-drain sequence completes without dropping >1% of in-flight requests in canary runs.
- Autoscaler respects reservations in at least 3 load profiles (steady, spike, slow decay).
- Cross-region spillover denies movement for customers without opt-in tags and logs audit evidence for allowed moves.
- Chaos-safe drain completes in staging and a non-disruptive run is scheduled in prod with metrics validated.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (week 1–2): API + console behind feature flag; unit/integration tests.
- Stage 2 (week 3): Orchestrator + autoscaler changes in canary region (us-west-2) with synthetic traffic and dedicated test tenants.
- Stage 3 (week 5): Controlled opt-in customer pilots; run chaos-safe drain weekly and collect metrics.
- Stage 4 (week 8): Gradual opt-out rollout to all dedicated pools with guardrails and emergency rollback.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New metrics: reserved_capacity_utilization, soft_drain_completion_time, eviction_error_rate, cross_region_spill_count.
- Alerts: resident_quota_breach (>95% for 10m), unexpected_eviction (>0.1% per minute for resident_quota), failed_audit_event.

Open questions / next steps:
- Finalize format for cryptographic residency proof (KMS attestation or signed token).
- Decide default resident_quota sizing heuristics for newly provisioned pools.
- UX: how granular should reservations be (per-customer vs per-route)?

Related artifacts: Confluence doc (design drafts), perf notes, and incident timeline from last region failover are linked in comments.

Estimated effort: 5 sprint points across infra/runtime/autoscale engineers with support from Console and Security for audit flows.
